roles.heroLead: Up here the weather tests everything, and a shower is no exception — tile and grout shrug water off, but only a bonded membrane actually stops it. Skip that layer and a North Bend bathroom quietly becomes a framing repair. We build the assembly, flood it for 24 hours, photograph it holding, then tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in North Bend, WA?
roles.costP1: In North Bend, installed tile runs about $14–$26 per square foot once you stack up tile, setting materials, substrate prep and the labor; labor starts at $11/sq ft by itself. Expect $3,200–$6,800 on a tub-shower surround, $900–$1,600 on a ~45 sq ft bathroom floor, and $6,500–$14,000 on a complete bathroom — floor, shower and niche together.
roles.costP2: Format is the lever most people miss. Installing a $4 mosaic can outprice installing a $12 large-format porcelain plank, since every cut and every grout joint is labor — the receipt from the tile aisle is the smaller half of the story.
roles.costNote: Upper-valley ranges as of August 2026, covering tile, materials and labor together. The free on-site estimate produces the written number that holds.
roles.layersLead: Count seven layers from subfloor to grout. Each failed shower we tear into skipped at least one — the membrane, almost every time — and the few hundred dollars it saved became a five-figure demolition.
roles.whyP1: A leak never knocks. Water sneaks through grout, soaks the substrate, and only after a winter or two does the evidence appear — a soft spot in the hall, a ring on the ceiling below. By then the job list reads framing, subfloor, drywall and tile, all over again.
roles.whyP2: About a tenth of what a shower costs is the waterproofing. Deleting that tenth is the costliest decision a remodel can make.

roles.cardFloors: Mudrooms, entries, kitchens and baths — floors that meet ski boots and firewood. Subfloor brought flat first, uncoupling membrane wherever movement or radiant heat calls for it.

roles.faqH2: Tile installation FAQ — North Bend, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in North Bend, WA?
roles.faqA1: Tile installation in North Bend prices at $14 to $26 per square foot installed, taking in the tile, its setting materials, the substrate prep and labor — the labor line alone from $11 per square foot. A typical tub-shower surround costs $3,200 to $6,800; a full bathroom holding floor, shower and niche finishes between $6,500 and $14,000. The format you pick moves cost more than the tile's sticker: mosaics and large-format each demand well more labor per foot than basic 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in North Bend?
roles.faqA2: $3,200 to $6,800 covers a standard alcove shower in North Bend — tear-out, bonded waterproofing, the sloped pan or base, tile work, niche and grout included. Curbless entries, benches, steam builds and full-height stone land above that. The waterproofing is about a tenth of the price and the whole reason the other nine-tenths survive.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes — it's the one step that never gets skipped. Every shower gets a bonded system behind the tile: a sloped base with the fall built in, an ANSI A118.10 membrane in sheet or liquid form taken up the walls with corners, seams and pipe penetrations sealed, and a full 24-hour flood test photographed before setting begins. Tile and grout only slow water down; stopping it is the membrane's job alone.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: A North Bend bathroom deserves four to six working days: day one, demolition behind dust protection; day two, substrate and waterproofing topped by 24 hours of flood testing; the middle stretch goes to setting tile; the finale is grout, silicone and trim. Grout wants another 24 hours of cure before that first shower. Floors by themselves are one-to-two-day projects.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain for floors, showers and any surface that gets wet or worked hard — it's denser, chips less and absorbs under 0.5% water, which matters in a house where boots come in wet half the year. Ceramic serves well on walls and backsplashes for less money. Our North Bend rule: porcelain underfoot, always; ceramic and glass up top where they belong.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — and up this end of the valley no upgrade beats its cost-to-comfort ratio. The rate is $11 to $16 per square foot covering mat, thermostat and install. Over an uncoupling membrane it goes; its resistance gets measured before tile and once more after; a dedicated circuit feeds it. The money only works with the floor already open, so fold it into the remodel plan — not the regret list.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, yes. Demo of old tile with haul-away opens near $3.50 per square foot; in exchange you get the only genuine subfloor look you'll ever have — rot, movement — plus finished heights that stay right at the doors. Sometimes a flat, sound, firmly bonded floor can accept tile on top, but the height rises while the unknowns stay buried. We'd rather face them at demo than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in North Bend?
roles.faqA8: For a standard 30 square foot kitchen, a North Bend backsplash installs at $1,100 to $2,200 — outlet openings cut in, edges finished with trim, grout tuned to the counter. Mosaic sheets, herringbone runs, a framed feature behind the stove and ceiling-height slab-look porcelain occupy the top end, because the hours live in layout and cutting.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, yes. From $8 per square foot we repair and regrout: stained or crumbling grout, the odd cracked tile from something dropped, corners where the old grout should give way to silicone. If tiles ring hollow, let go in a spreading pattern, or the wall flexes, the substrate underneath has failed — a repair there only rents time. You'll hear which diagnosis is yours before we price anything.
roles.faqQ10: Which North Bend neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: The whole upper valley — downtown North Bend, Si View, Forster Woods, Tanner, Riverbend, Wilderness Rim, Cedar Falls, Edgewick, Maloney Grove and Sallal Prairie — plus Snoqualmie, Snoqualmie Ridge, Fall City, Preston and on up toward Snoqualmie Pass. Ernie's Grove and the far side of the valley too; just say where you are.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Workmanship on tile is warranted 2 years by OC Flooring — noticeably past our carpet coverage, for problems that show up around year two instead of right away. Install the complete bonded assembly and the manufacturer's warranty travels with it. Photographs of membrane and flood test outlast the remodel itself — documentation that moves with the house.
